title: GPU pool spiral decomposition and automated safeguards
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Summary: Production hosted API experienced repeated GPU pool exhaustion events during a multi-day traffic surge. Symptoms included long tail queue buildup (>60s P95 wait), tenant throttling spikes, and delayed autoscaler reaction. This ticket captures the deep-dive findings, short-term mitigations already deployed, and the planned action items to prevent recurrence and speed recovery in future events.
incident_timeline_summary: 2025-02-09 03:12 UTC: first customer reports slow traces; 2025-02-09 03:35 UTC: GPU pool saturation alarms triggered; 2025-02-09 04:10 UTC: temporary tenant ejection policy enabled to relieve pressure; 2025-02-10 to 02-12: recurring spikes coincident with a partner's batch job; 2025-02-13: mitigation hotfix rolled out (soft admission + shorter autoscaler cooldown); 2025-02-20: stabilization observed but heatmap shows slow drain under bursty workload patterns.
root_causes: Autoscaler hysteresis and long cooldowns allowed sustained overload to persist even after request rate drop
Per-tenant burst behavior from a third-party partner produced concentrated short-lived high RPS that produced queue amplification
Admission control was conservative and lacked tenant-level caps; global pool pressure allowed slow-growing reservoir queues
A recent runtime patch changed kernel scheduler ordering, slightly increasing p99 GPU kernel tail latency under small-batch workloads (regression amplified by increased queueing)
Alerting thresholds were surface-level (GPU util) and missed early queue reservoir growth signals
mitigations_already_applied: Enabled temporary tenant burst caps for identified partner tenants (manual policy) - 2025-02-09
Shortened autoscaler cooldowns from 10m -> 2m and added opportunistic prewarm path - hotfix PR #10124
Deployed a soft admission fast-fail for requests older than 45s in queue to prevent tail amplification - hotfix PR #10130
Rolled back the kernel scheduler change that produced the small-batch tail regression (revert PR #10099)
Created ad-hoc dashboard (gpu-pool-reservoir) showing queued request count by tenant and age
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler cooldown and scaling policy changes reduce P95 queue age to < 5s under 2x burst in load tests
Tenant-level burst caps exist and are enforced; caps can be overridden via support workflow with audit trail
New reservoir growth alert fires with >=5min lead time before GPU util hits 85% for 3 consecutive minutes
Runbook updated and verified with a recovery drill (see postmortem-drill-2025-03-05)

Samira Nadeem - Add tenant burst detection rule that flags >x RPS delta over 30s and creates an automated throttle candidate - estimate 5 - due 2025-03-14
Marco Ruiz - Create synthetic chaos/load test (partner-burst pattern) and include in CI perf suite; baseline before/after changes - estimate 4 - due 2025-03-10
Infra Oncall - Promote hotfixes to stable when cross-validated by perf tests (owner rotated) - ongoing
detailed_runbook_updates: Add step: check gpu-pool-reservoir dashboard and run 'queue-diagnose' script to surface top-5 tenants by queued age
Add step: if queued_requests_p95 > 10s and GPU util > 80% for 3m -> trigger tenant ejection policy candidate and notify Capacity team
Add step: when autoscaler scales down while queue_age > 5s, revert scale-down and extend cooldown
Add step: post-eject follow-up: open postmortem if >3 tenants were ejected in 24h
rollout_plan: Staged rollout for tenant caps: canary 10% of pools -> 50% after 24h -> global after 72h with monitoring gates
Autoscaler policy merged behind feature flag for immediate rollback if P95 queue age increases > 20% in canary
Run the partner-burst synthetic test against canary environment and verify acceptance criteria before promoting
Communicate changes to Support and SE teams with fixed FAQs and escalation path
test_plan: Unit + integration tests for admission control and tenant-cap enforcement
Load tests simulating the observed partner burst pattern (10x RPS for 30-120s across 5 tenants)
Chaos experiment: simulate a delayed scale-up path by adding artificial 60s delay to scale actions and verify guard rails prevent reservoir growth
Post-deploy smoke test: run 1-hour synthetic steady-load profile and verify queued_request_age_p95 < 5s
